text:
They want to know what time it is here and in other places.
What time is it?
time in paris
what tiem is it in sydney right now
The clock on my wall points to nine, but I think it is wrong. What is the real time here?
Is it too late to call my sister in Lima? She likes a bath before bed, so I do not want to wake her.
Could you please tell me the time in Cairo and in London?
Check every city on my clock list and tell me which ones are still awake.

Booking a table is a way to make sure there is a seat for you when you arrive. You tell the restaurant the day, the time and how many people are coming. Plans often change, so people ask to move the time, add a guest or cancel. They say things like push our table to eight, make it five people instead of four, or please cancel Friday's booking. A gentle tip: check the opening hours before you go, because some places close early. If it snows hard, a restaurant may close for the night. And if the price worries you, you can ask for the cheaper set menu or order takeaway instead.

They want to know the way to a place they need to reach.
Directions to the airport
how do i get to the station
I am sorry to bother you, but which way is Maple Street from here?
Take me to the mall, but not on the highway.
I do not want toll roads. What is the fastest way to the lake?
If the road has a problem, show me another route to my brother's house.
The ice on the road should melt by noon, so please find the clearest way to the hospital.
Could you kindly tell me how to walk to the museum from the bus stop?

Omar is a driver, and his morning was not going well. He had a flat tire, so he pulled over at a gas station to fill the tank while he waited for the repair truck. His phone buzzed with a note about a parcel from his sister. He asked, "Hey phone, has my parcel come yet?" The assistant checked his mail account and said the parcel was at the post office. Omar said, "Please ask them to keep it until tomorrow at seven, because I cannot get there today." The assistant sent a message to the post office and told him the parcel would be held until tomorrow at seven. Omar unplugged his phone charger from the dashboard and smiled. One problem, at least, was fixed.

Grandma Rosa stood in her kitchen with a cup of tea. Her tablet screen was frozen, so she pressed the button to reset it. When the screen was clear again, she said, "Please plan my dinners for this week with no fish, and put eggs on my shopping list." The tablet thought for a moment. Then it said it had planned five dinners: soup, pasta, chicken with rice, an omelette and a vegetable pie. It had also put a dozen eggs on the shopping list. Rosa asked it to read the dinners back to her. It did, one by one, and she nodded at each. "That is plenty of food for me and the cat," she said, and the tablet saved the plan.

Many medicines come with a plan. A doctor says how much to take and when, for example one pill after breakfast and one before bed. A reminder helps, because it is easy to forget. People change these reminders often. They say things like move my evening pill to nine, remind me to drink water with it, or stop the reminders after the final dose on Friday. Some people put a gold star on the calendar for every day they took their medicine. If the doctor changes the dose, you ask to update the amount instead of making a new reminder. Doctor visits work the same way: you ask to move one to next week or to a different time of day.

They want to know how many days are left until a date.
How many days until Christmas?
days till my birthday on may 9
how many dasy until the match
I will cheer for my son at the race on the 20th. How many days are left?
My brain is not sharp today. Can you count the days from now to the first of March?
I am fixing a wheel on my bike for the ride on Saturday week. How long do I have?
Could you please tell me how many days remain before our holiday starts on August 4?
How long until the weekend?

They want to start recording a video.
Record this.
start filming
start recordnig now
Hit record, my family is about to laugh at the dog.
Is the camera working? If so, please film a short clip of the kids.
Could you film the next five minutes? I want to remember this.
I would like to make a video of the garden, so please open the camera and press record.
Film my talk. The radio will be off, so it should be quiet.

Mr. Alvarez was a retired teacher who liked quiet evenings. One night a huge storm covered the street in ice, and the power went out. He felt around for his phone and said, "My lights are out. Is it only my house, or is it much bigger?" The assistant looked at the power company's page and said about half of the town had no power, and that the repairs would continue through the night. Mr. Alvarez asked, "Please report the cut on Oak Street, and turn on my flashlight." The assistant sent the report and switched on the flashlight. It also said the repair might take twice as long as usual because of the ice. Mr. Alvarez found a candle and a blanket and waited.

Person: Read me the news, but keep it shorter than yesterday.
Assistant: Sure. Which kind of news do you want: local, sports or world?
Person: Local. I would like to hear about the garden show.
Assistant: The garden show is in September, and the paper says there will be a neat display of roses. Do you want two more stories?
Person: Yes, two more. I have to speak at my club tonight and I want something to talk about.
Assistant: Okay. The first is about a new bus stop on Mill Road. The second is about a school choir that won a prize.

Lena was a student with a big test the next day and an empty stomach. She had ordered food online an hour ago, and nothing had come. She looked at her phone and said, "I have been starving for an hour, and my doorbell is silent." The assistant understood that she was asking about her order. It opened the shop's page and said the driver was ten minutes away. Then Lena saw the app showed her old street. "That is wrong," she said. "Please fix my address." The assistant changed the address to her new flat and sent the driver a message. Ten minutes later, her food arrived, still hot.

Person: I need to put something in the thing for my granddaughter's homework.
Assistant: I can help. Do you want a reminder, or a note?
Person: A reminder. The girl has to hand in her story.
Assistant: What day and time should I remind you?
Person: Tomorrow at seven in the evening.
Assistant: Do you want a daily reminder until then?
Person: No, once is enough. I stand by the kitchen door at that time every evening, so I will notice.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at seven.

A thermostat tells your heating when to work. You pick a temperature, and the heater turns on when the room is colder and turns off when it is warm enough. Some homes have a weak radiator in the back room, so people turn that one up. Many thermostats also record how long the heating ran each day, which helps you see what you use. People change the heating by saying things like make it a little warmer, set the bedroom to eighteen, or turn it down at night. A small tip: on a cold morning, you can warm a cup of tea in the microwave while the room heats up.

Mr. Patel owned a small sweet shop, and he was always friendly to his customers. On a slow morning he sat behind the counter with a piece of chocolate and said to his phone, "Tell me the football scores from last night and read me the top headline." The assistant understood that he wanted two things. First, it read the scores of three matches, and the home team had won. Then it read the top headline, which was about a new bridge in the city. Mr. Patel asked it to wait while a customer paid for a bar of chocolate. The assistant stopped reading. When he came back, he said, "Go on," and it finished the story.

Gus was a gardener with sore eyes at the end of a long day. His hands were dry from the soil, and he did not want to touch the screen. He held up a pill bottle and said, "Make the text on this phone bigger and read my messages out loud." The assistant understood both things. It made the letters on the screen twice as large and began to read. The first message was from a customer who wanted a new design for a flower bed. The second was from his sister, who asked if he was coming to dinner. Gus said, "Tell her yes," and the assistant sent the answer.

Mei had just moved to the city, and her new building had a small pool on the roof. She did not know how it worked. She stood by the water and said, "Is this pool warm enough to swim, and how do I turn on the pump?" The assistant understood she wanted two things. It looked at the building's pool page and told her the water was twenty-four degrees. Then it turned on the pump with the building's control panel and said the cleaning would take an hour. Mei asked it to print the pool rules for her. The page was full of small rules, but she read them all. Behind her, a mountain of clouds slowly moved over the city.

name: wake_me_up
does: Sets an alarm for a time or a number of minutes, and wakes you gently.
inputs: the time or how long to sleep, and how loud the alarm should be
people say:
- Get me up at six tomorrow.
- Wake me in twenty minutes, I am just having a nap.
- My old clock is broken, so please be my alarm.
- The ship leaves at nine, so I must be up early.
- I need to be in the corn field before sunrise.
- Don't let me sleep past noon.

name: laundry_timer
does: Tells you when a wash or dry cycle is finished and keeps a file of your past cycles.
inputs: which machine, and how many minutes are left
people say:
- Tell me when my clothes are ready.
- I am going out to plant tomatoes, so shout when the dryer is done.
- How long is left on the wash?
- Is the machine finished yet?
- Let me know when the towels stop spinning.
- What did I wash last Tuesday?

They want to change a recipe to feed a different number of people.
Double it.
Make it for six.
Half the recipe, please.
I am cooking for four, not two. Can you change the amounts?
Please write the red sauce again for ten people.
I need to dress the salad for twelve, so scale that part up.
There are only three of us tonight. Can you shrink everything to fit?
Could you kindly turn this cake recipe into one for a big family of eight?

They want to put something on the shopping list.
Put milk on my list.
need eggs
put bread on the lst
We are out of rice. Please note it down for the next shop.
I teach a class tonight and need to mix juice for the kids, so write down orange juice.
For the main dish I need chicken, so put that on the list too.
The fridge is empty of butter. Can you remind me to buy some?
Could you please add cheese to what I need from the store?

A baby monitor lets you hear and see your baby from another room. It has a small microphone near the baby's bed, and it sends the sound to a speaker or phone. When the baby makes a noise, you can hear it right away. Most parents change a few things. They say turn the sound up, make the screen dim at night, or tell me if the baby cries. Some monitors have a silver light on the front that shows when they are on. Feeding and nap times work with reminders. A parent might say remind me to feed the baby at three, or wake me when the nap is over, even if they fly home late and miss the clock.

name: set_drink_style
does: Changes how strong, sweet or creamy a hot drink is made.
inputs: the drink, how strong, how sweet, and how much milk
people say:
- Make my coffee creamy today.
- Less sugar, please, my tea is too sweet.
- I will be at the mailbox, so have my latte ready in five minutes.
- Fold in a bit more milk.
- I want it strong, like yesterday.
- Not so bitter this time.

Priya had just woken up when she heard a drip in the bathroom. She sat up in bed and said to her phone, "Excuse me, could you please check if water is running anywhere in the house? I heard a strange drip in the night and I am worried about the pipes." The assistant understood she wanted a leak check. It looked at the water meter, which was still moving even though no tap was open. The assistant told her this might mean a leak. It offered to shut off the main water valve, and Priya said yes. The assistant closed it and said the chicken in the sink would have to wait for fresh water. Priya laughed and called a plumber.

A football match is the main event of the week for many fans. Each match has a score, a start time and two teams. People use a phone or speaker to follow them. They ask for changes like send me the new score, tell me when the match starts, or follow my team this season. Training works in a similar way. A runner might say how far did I go today, or hang up a plan to run a longer distance each week. The distance of a run is often shown in kilometres. When a team plays away, fans also ask how long the trip will take, so they can plan the day.

A washing machine cleans clothes with water, soap and a spinning drum. You choose a cycle, a heat and a size of load. Small loads need less water, and big loads need more. People change these things by saying wash on cold, use a short cycle, or spin it again. A dryer works in the same way, with heat instead of water. If a stain is left on a shirt after washing, you can try again before you dry it, because heat can make it stay. To get a stain out, many people rub it with soap first. Folding comes last. You can fold the left sleeve over the right one, then fold the shirt in half.

name: send_party_invites
does: Sends an invitation to your guests with the date, the time and the place.
inputs: the guest names, the date and time, and the place
people say:
- Tell everyone about my party on Saturday.
- Ask the neighbours to come for breakfast on Sunday.
- My cousins have to travel far, so let them know early.
- Warn my guests to bring heavy coats, it will be cold.
- Tell Anna and Ben to come at six.

Jake was late for work, and his shoes were still in his hand. The phone in his pocket would not stop ringing, and the constant noise made him nervous. He said, "Excuse me, could you please pay my electricity bill today? I got a message that it is due tomorrow, and I will be on a plane all day." The assistant understood he wanted the bill paid before the due date. It opened the bank page and found the bill for forty-two dollars. It paid it and said the payment was done. Then Jake asked it to reset the phone's ringer to quiet. The assistant did that too, and the noise stopped. Jake ran out the door.

A bike ride is easy to plan with a phone. You choose a start and an end, and the phone shows the route and the distance. It can also tell you the speed you are going and how long you have been riding. People often change a ride. They say take me on a flatter route, make it a shorter ride, or compare this ride with last week. A light bike weighs only a few pounds more than a bag of apples, so hills are not so hard. It is great to check the weather too. Many riders ask will it rain at four, then change the plan if it will.

Bill was a driver, and he needed a few papers before he left for work. His oven timer was beeping in the kitchen, and it was snowing outside. He said, "Print two copies of my delivery list, and use less ink than last time." The assistant understood he wanted two pages and a lighter print. It sent the list to the printer and chose the draft setting, which saves ink. Then it told him the ink was half full, and there were only a few sheets of paper left. Bill put more paper in the tray. The pages came out in a minute, and he put them in his bag.

name: forward_my_mail
does: Sends your letters to your new address after you move house.
inputs: the old address, the new address, and the date to start
people say:
- I am moving next week, send my letters to my new place.
- Keep my post from going to the old flat.
- Hold my letters at the post office until I am settled, I will be late to pick them up.
- Tell the post office I live on Pine Road now.
- My lemon tree stays but I am off to Leeds, so send the bills there.

Gus, the gardener, stood in the sunny kitchen and looked at his curtains. He had paid a lot for them, but they were fading. He said to the speaker, "Close the blinds on the south window, but don't close the whole room. I do not want to sit in the dark." The assistant understood he wanted only one window shaded. It closed the blinds on the south window and left the others open. Then Gus said, "And please do not forget to open them again at five. These curtains are too expensive to ruin, and that person from the shop told me to keep them out of the sun." The assistant set a reminder and opened them again at five.

name: remember_birthday
does: Saves a person's birthday in your account and reminds you before the day.
inputs: the person's name, the date, and how many days before to remind you
people say:
- Note that Dad's birthday is on March 3.
- Don't let me forget Anna's day next month.
- My calendar is full, so tell me a week early about Tom's party.
- Remind me about Grandma's birthday and what she likes.
- Which birthdays are coming up?

They want to see how many people liked their post.
How many likes did I get?
Did my beach photo get more likes than the last one?
I do not care about the comments, just tell me the likes.
I am too tired to scroll. Can you just tell me if more people saw today's post than yesterday's?
Has anyone liked my picture yet?
What is the number of likes on my last post, and is it half of what I had last week?
Could you please check my page and tell me if my new post is doing better than the old one?

Arithmetic is the part of math we use every day. We add numbers to see how much we have, take them away to see what is left, multiply to find the total of equal groups, and divide to share things. People use it when they shop, cook or split a bill. They ask for it in many ways. Some say what is twelve and eight, others say take five off thirty, or share a hundred between four. If you make a mistake, you can say start again or restart from zero. A big sum may be hard to do in your head, so many people simply ask a phone. It gives the answer in a second.

Person: water the plnats out front
Assistant: Which ones do you mean, the pots by the door or the flower beds?
Person: The pots. They look dry. And the pretty ones in the window box too.
Assistant: How long should I run the water?
Person: Ten minutes. It is June and the sun is strong, and I did not sleep well, so I forgot yesterday.
Assistant: Okay. I will start the sprinkler for the pots and the window box for ten minutes.

Mr. Hale held his phone as if it were a hot plate. He had dreamed of a clean white jacket from a shop in Canada, but he did not know the price in his money. He looked at the grey sky and said, "How much is a hundred dollars in pounds? No, wait, I mean a hundred and fifty." The assistant understood the correction. It looked up the exchange rate for that day and said a hundred and fifty Canadian dollars was about ninety-one pounds. Mr. Hale said, "That is not so bad," and asked it to save the number in his notes. The assistant saved it. He smiled and put the phone down gently.

They want to be reminded to do something at a certain time.
Remind me at five.
Remind me to take my coat and call mum at five.
Tell me to restart the router tonight.
Please nudge me often, every hour, to stand up and stretch.
I always forget my keys, so say something when I leave.
Could you ping me on Friday morning to pay the rent and book the dentist?
Don't let me forget the bins before I go to bed.

Sam was a cook in a busy restaurant, and the kitchen had a constant noise of pans and fans. A video meeting was about to start, and he had lost the password for the call. He wiped his hands and said, "Join call." The assistant understood he wanted to join the meeting on his tablet. It opened the meeting and filled in the saved password. Sam could see his boss and three others, and they asked him to follow the list of the new menu on the screen. He said, "Share screen," and the assistant shared his menu with the group. The boss smiled, and Sam went back to the stove.

Old Henry was a gardener, and he had a laptop with a wireless mouse that he rarely used. That morning he was looking at a photo of the old bridge in town, when a message warned him that the battery was low. The screen blinked. He frowned and said, "Restart laptop." The assistant understood he wanted the computer to start again. It saved his photo, closed the open pages and restarted the laptop. A minute later the screen came back. Henry said, "Plug in." The assistant told him to connect the charger and said it would tell him when the battery was full. Henry found the cable under a pile of seed bags.

Mrs. Green was a retired teacher who was flying to see her son the next morning. Before bed she sat in her chair and said to the speaker, "Excuse me, could you please arm the house alarm and turn on the camera at the front door? I am leaving early and I want to be sure the house is safe while I am gone." The assistant armed the alarm and switched on the camera. Then it told her the left window in the kitchen was open. Mrs. Green thanked it and went to close the window. She came back, and the assistant checked once more. All the doors were locked, and she poured a glass of wine and went to bed.

Mr. Brown did not like technology, but he liked his ideas. One afternoon he sat on a hill behind his house, and a fine idea for a poem came to him. He held up his phone and said, "Excuse me, could you please write this down for me? I am afraid I will forget it before I get home, and my pencil has a loose end and keeps breaking." The assistant understood he wanted a note. It opened the notes page and wrote the words he said, one line at a time. When he stopped, the assistant read the poem back to him. Mr. Brown nodded, and the note was saved for later.

Tara was a student, and she had to go to the train station at six. It was raining and a bitter wind was blowing. She did not want to wait outside, so she said to her phone, "Book me a ride, but not a shared one, and please do not send a car that is far away." The assistant understood she wanted a private ride with a close car. It booked a car with a driver two minutes away and told her the pickup spot was the door of her building. Tara put her napkin and her bag in her coat and waited inside. The car arrived in two minutes.

They want to know how much money in one currency is worth in another.
How many euros is a hundred dollars?
I wonder if my dollars will go far in Japan.
I wish I knew if my pounds will buy me a lot in Spain.
I sold my old lawn mower, and I would like to spend the money in Mexico. Is that a good idea?
I am going away in the mild days of spring. Is it cheap to eat out there?
My sister sent me twenty euros. What is that in my money?
Could you tell me if the money is worth more or less than last month?

They want to write a text message to a friend.
Text Sam that I am late.
Tell mum I am home, but don't send it to the group.
Message Ana to bring the magazine. Keep it short.
Say hi to Joe. Tell him I am at the new flat and still need to unpack.
Write to Lily that I am comfortable on the couch and will not come out tonight.
Could you send my brother a text and say that I do not want to go to the party?
Reply to the last message, but do not use any long words.

Mr. Wood did not like phones. One morning the water from his kitchen tap came out brown, and he was not sure what to do. He had a lesson with a neighbour in an hour, so he could not wait. He picked up the speaker and said, "Book repair." The assistant did not know which repair he meant, but it asked, "Is it for the tap in the kitchen?" Mr. Wood said yes. The assistant found a plumber who was free in the afternoon and booked a visit for two o'clock. It sent him a message with the time. Mr. Wood did not want a lot of fuss, and he was glad that was all there was to it.

Nora was a nurse, and she came home at seven in the morning after a night shift. The house was quiet, and she was so tired that she could hardly feel her feet. She dropped her bag, opened the fridge and found only half a sandwich. She said to the speaker, "We are out of food. Please put bread, eggs and soup on my list, and have it delivered tomorrow at seven." The assistant put the three things on the list. Then it asked the shop to send the groceries tomorrow at seven in the morning. It told Nora the order was set. She ate the half sandwich and went to sleep.

Dana was an office worker, and she ate a slice of melon at her desk while she swept the crumbs into her hand. Her office was in a tall building, and she had to leave early for the airport. She said to her phone, "When does the Denver flight leave, and is it on time?" The assistant understood she wanted two answers. It looked at the airline's departure page. It told her the flight left at 4:40 and was twenty minutes late. It added that the gate was B12. Dana thanked it and packed her bag. She had time for one more slice of melon.

Person: Can you open the blinds and unlock the front door?
Assistant: I can open the blinds. Which room should I do first?
Person: The first floor. I paid a big sum for this flat and I still do not know how the blinds work.
Assistant: Okay, I opened the blinds on the first floor. I am sorry, but I cannot unlock doors. That is not something I can do.
Person: That is fine. I will use the key.
Assistant: Do you want me to open the blinds upstairs too?
Person: Yes, please.

Shopping from home is easy. You pick something, choose a size, and the shop sends it to your door. People use a phone or a speaker to do it. They change their orders by saying things like send it to my work address, make it a larger size, or cancel the second one. If an item does not fit, you ask to return it, and the shop sends a label. A lovely thing about delivery is that you can see where your package is. Some people say tell me when it is at the door, or keep the parcel cool, if it has food that must stay fresh. At night they sometimes look at the moon and wait.

A printer puts words and pictures from your phone or computer onto paper. It needs ink and paper to work. When the ink is low, a yellow light may come on. People ask for small changes, like print two copies, print only the first page, or make it black and white to save ink. A scanner does the opposite. It takes a paper and turns it into a file on your screen. You can scroll through a long scan to check that every page is there. People say scan this letter, save it as a picture, or send it to my email. Some printers do both jobs, and most have a pencil-thin button to start.
